interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 includes a wired, well-formed quiz gate after act_search_trace with a real question, plausible options, and a marked correct answer, whereas Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functioning interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 provides clear, natural narration with spoken math and no obvious TTS defects, while Lesson 1 has no transcript available, making its narration absent and therefore worse on this dimension.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 provides visual cues that are generally timed to the narrated references, while Lesson 1 has no transcript or cue timing at all, making synchronization absent and unevaluable.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 accurately traces binary search to index 7 and clearly explains the halving/logarithmic reasoning, while Lesson 1 has no available transcript or lesson content to verify or teach the concept at all.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has a cleaner, more consistent slide-style layout with legible text and centered presentation, while Lesson 1 is dominated by browser/chat UI clutter, excessive empty space, off-center/tiny lesson content, and overlapping interface elements.

aggregator.explanation: Five of the six high-confidence dimension agents favored Lesson 2: it had functioning interactivity, clear narration, better synchronization, stronger concept explanation, and more polished presentation. Lesson 1 decisively won visual accuracy because its binary search visualization was correct while Lesson 2 contained visual/formula issues, but Lesson 1 lacked transcript, timing, and interactivity evidence across most other dimensions. Overall, the confident majority supports Lesson 2 despite its visual accuracy flaws.
